# Python API reference

Every name the `platoon` package exports, with its signature and docstring. Import the package as `pt`:

```python
import platoon as pt
```

Signatures are written as in the source, so annotations name types by their source names (for example `Task` is `pt.Task`).

This page is generated from the docstrings of the names `platoon` exports by `scripts/gen_reference.py`. To change it, edit the code and run `python scripts/gen_reference.py`; `tests/docs/test_reference_up_to_date.py` fails while the page is stale. The commands, config keys and names documented here are platoon's public contract: changing, renaming or removing one starts as an RFC (see [when a change needs an RFC](../../CONTRIBUTING.md#when-a-change-needs-an-rfc) and [the RFC process](../rfcs/README.md)).

| Name | Summary |
|---|---|
| [`pt.harness`](#pt-harness) | Register the decorated `async def fn(ctx: AgentContext) -> AgentResult` as harness `name@version`. |

| [`pt.get_harness`](#pt-get-harness) | Resolve `name[@version]`, a `.toml` path or a `module:function` reference to a `HarnessSpec` or a `FunctionHarness`. |

## Harnesses

A harness is agent code. A function harness is an async function registered with `@pt.harness`; TOML harness specs describe command-line agents. Environment configs name either kind by `name[@version]`.

<a id="pt-harness"></a>

### `pt.harness`

```python
def harness(
    name: str,
    *,
    version: str = "1",
    runtime: Runtime = "inline",
    executes_model_code: bool = False,
) -> Callable[[AgentFn], AgentFn]
```

Register the decorated `async def fn(ctx: AgentContext) -> AgentResult` as harness `name@version`.

Environment configs then name it like a TOML harness spec (`harness: name`).  The name follows platoon's
naming rule (`platoon.extensions`): lower case, `<owner>-<name>`, with `platoon-*` reserved for core.
`runtime="inline"`, the only runtime, runs the function in the rollout worker's event loop.
`executes_model_code` declares that the harness runs code the model wrote; it is recorded with every
rollout.  The decorator returns the function unchanged:

    @pt.harness("my-agent", version="2")
    async def my_agent(ctx: pt.AgentContext) -> pt.AgentResult:
        reply = await ctx.chat([{"role": "user", "content": ctx.instruction}])
        return pt.AgentResult("completed", final_message=reply.text)

<a id="pt-functionharness"></a>

### `pt.FunctionHarness`

```python
class FunctionHarness
```

A harness implemented by an async Python function (`platoon.harness.agent.AgentFn`).

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `str` | required |  |
| `version` | `str` | required |  |
| `runtime` | `Runtime` | required | Where the function runs; `inline` runs it in the rollout worker's event loop. |
| `executes_model_code` | `bool` | required | The harness runs code the model wrote. |
| `fn` | `AgentFn` | required | The decorated function. |
| `ref` | `str` | | `name@version`, the key environment configs and trajectories use. Read-only. |
| `source` | `str` | | `module:qualname` of the function. Read-only. |

<a id="pt-get-harness"></a>

### `pt.get_harness`

```python
def get_harness(ref: str) -> Harness
```

Resolve `name[@version]`, a `.toml` path or a `module:function` reference to a `HarnessSpec` or a
`FunctionHarness`.

A name is a built-in's, an installed `platoon.harnesses` entry point's (imported the first time it is
named), or one a `package` module registered.  Raises `platoon.extensions.ExtensionError` (a
`ValueError`) when nothing, or more than one harness, matches.

## The agent contract

What a function harness sees while it runs one agent: the `AgentContext` it receives, the `AgentResult` it returns, and the types around them. Every model call goes through the model gateway and is recorded on the agent for training.

<a id="pt-agentcontext"></a>

### `pt.AgentContext`

```python
class AgentContext(Protocol)
```

What a function harness gets for one agent.

| Attribute | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `agent_id` | `str` | This agent's id. |
| `trajectory_id` | `str` | The id of the trajectory this agent's calls are recorded on. |
| `parent_agent_id` | `str \| None` | The parent agent's id (None for the root). |
| `depth` | `int` | Depth in the agent tree; the root is 0. |
| `role` | `str` | The agent's role: `policy` for the root, the `role` its spawn named for a child (default `subagent`). |
| `task` | `Task` | The task the agent works on. |
| `session` | `EnvSession` | The environment session the agent acts on. |
| `instruction` | `str` | The goal the agent works on. |
| `max_steps` | `int \| None` | The agent's step limit (None: only the budget limits it). |
| `access` | `ToolAccess` | The agent's tool access. |
| `options` | `Mapping[str, Any]` | Harness options from the environment config (or the spawn call). |
| `endpoint` | `ModelEndpoint` | The agent's model endpoint over HTTP; calls through it are recorded on this agent exactly like `chat`. |
| `mcp` | `McpEndpoint \| None` | The agent's tools over MCP, set when the gateway serves them. |
| `budget` | `Budget` | The agent's step budget. |
| `agents` | `AgentAPI` | Subagents: `ctx.agents.spawn`. |

#### `AgentContext.chat`

```python
async def chat(
    messages: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]],
    *,
    tools: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]] | None = None,
    kind: str = "policy",
    **sampling: Any,
) -> ChatReply
```

One model call, recorded on this agent; `sampling` takes Chat Completions parameters.

#### `AgentContext.list_tools`

```python
async def list_tools() -> list[ToolSpec]
```

The env's tools, filtered by this agent's access.

#### `AgentContext.call_tool`

```python
async def call_tool(name: str, arguments: Mapping[str, Any]) -> ToolResult
```

Call an env tool; a tool outside this agent's access returns an error result.

#### `AgentContext.annotate`

```python
def annotate(**misc: Any) -> None
```

Merge `misc` into this agent's trajectory misc.

#### `AgentContext.annotate_step`

```python
def annotate_step(**misc: Any) -> None
```

Merge `misc` into the step misc of the last call recorded on this agent.

`exclude_from_training=True` keeps that call out of the training data (the step stays for viewers).

<a id="pt-agentresult"></a>

### `pt.AgentResult`

```python
class AgentResult
```

How a harness run ended.

`completed`: the harness finished (the env grades the outcome, not this status); `limit`: it ran out of
steps; `timeout`/`cancelled`: it was interrupted; `error`: it failed, with `error` saying why.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `status` | `AgentStatus` | `"completed"` |  |
| `final_message` | `str \| None` | `None` | The agent's final answer, if it gave one. |
| `error` | `str \| None` | `None` | Why the run failed or stopped early. |

<a id="pt-agentstatus"></a>

### `pt.AgentStatus`

```python
AgentStatus = Literal["completed", "limit", "timeout", "error", "cancelled"]
```

How a harness run ended (`AgentResult.status`).

<a id="pt-agentfn"></a>

### `pt.AgentFn`

```python
AgentFn = Callable[..., Awaitable[AgentResult]]
```

A function harness: `async def fn(ctx: AgentContext) -> AgentResult`; options arrive as `ctx.options`.

<a id="pt-chatreply"></a>

### `pt.ChatReply`

```python
class ChatReply
```

One recorded model call: the assistant message (`content`, `tool_calls`, `reasoning_content`).

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `call_id` | `str` | required | The id of the recorded call. |
| `message` | `Mapping[str, Any]` | required | The assistant message, in Chat Completions form. |
| `finish_reason` | `str` | required | Why generation stopped, for example `stop`, `length` or `tool_calls`. |
| `text` | `str` | | The visible text of the reply ("" when the model only called tools). Read-only. |
| `reasoning` | `str \| None` | | The model's reasoning text, when the renderer separates it from the reply. Read-only. |
| `tool_calls` | `Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]]` | | OpenAI tool calls (`{"id", "type": "function", "function": {"name", "arguments"}}`), possibly empty. Read-only. |

<a id="pt-budget"></a>

### `pt.Budget`

```python
class Budget(Protocol)
```

The agent's step budget: one step is one `policy` call recorded on the agent.

#### `Budget.remaining`

```python
def remaining() -> float
```

Steps this agent may still take (`inf` when unbounded); reserved child budgets are subtracted.

#### `Budget.used`

```python
def used() -> float
```

<a id="pt-agentapi"></a>

### `pt.AgentAPI`

```python
class AgentAPI(Protocol)
```

Subagents: `ctx.agents.spawn` runs a child agent to completion and returns its `SubagentResult`.

#### `AgentAPI.spawn`

```python
async def spawn(
    goal: str,
    *,
    harness: str | None = None,
    max_steps: int | None = None,
    fork: ForkMode | None = None,
    access: ToolAccess | None = None,
    role: str = "subagent",
    options: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    task_misc: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> SubagentResult
```

Run `goal` in a child agent.

Unset arguments come from the environment's `agents` config and the parent: the same harness and
options, the env's fork mode, the configured child access and step budget.  Concurrent spawns are
allowed (`asyncio.gather`); each reserves its budget atomically.

Cancelling the call cancels the child and gives its budget back, unless `keep_children` was called.
A call still running when the parent's harness ends (say an un-awaited `asyncio.gather` of spawns) keeps
its child: the parent waits for it to finish and be graded, and cancels it only when the parent itself is
cancelled or times out, which includes a harness that returns `AgentResult("timeout")`.

#### `AgentAPI.keep_children`

```python
def keep_children() -> None
```

Keep the children of spawn calls cancelled from now on: they run on, and the parent waits for them to
finish and be graded before it ends.

For a harness that cancels its pending calls on its way out but wants the children they launched to
finish, as CodeAct does before it closes its cell loop (an un-awaited `asyncio.gather` of launches).

<a id="pt-subagentresult"></a>

### `pt.SubagentResult`

```python
class SubagentResult
```

What a parent gets back from `ctx.agents.spawn`.

A child never raises into its parent: a rejected launch (depth or budget) or a failed child comes back with
a non-`completed` `result` and a failure text in `message`.  `outcome` is the child's own grade (its
forked env session's grade, or its verifier's verdict), or None when the child was not graded.  A rejected
launch opened no agent, so its `agent_id` and `trajectory_id` are empty.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `agent_id` | `str` | required | The child agent's id ("" for a rejected launch). |
| `trajectory_id` | `str` | required | The id of the child's trajectory ("" for a rejected launch). |
| `goal` | `str` | required | The goal the child was given. |
| `result` | `AgentResult` | required | How the child's harness run ended. |
| `outcome` | `Outcome \| None` | required |  |
| `message` | `str` | required | The child's final message, or the failure text. |
| `launched` | `bool` | | Whether a child agent ran (False for launches rejected by the depth limit or the budget). Read-only. |
| `ok` | `bool` | | Whether the child ran and its harness completed (its grade is in `outcome`). Read-only. |

<a id="pt-modelendpoint"></a>

### `pt.ModelEndpoint`

```python
class ModelEndpoint
```

The agent's model endpoint, for harnesses with their own HTTP client (OpenAI SDK, litellm, OpenHands).

`base_url` is OpenAI-compatible and ends in `/v1`; it is already scoped to this agent (the secret is in
the path), so calls through it are recorded on the agent exactly like `ctx.chat`.  `api_key` is the agent
key, for clients that insist on sending one.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `base_url` | `str` | required |  |
| `api_key` | `str` | required |  |
| `model` | `str` | required | The model name to send in requests. |

#### `ModelEndpoint.headers`

```python
def headers(kind: str = "policy") -> dict[str, str]
```

Extra request headers that mark calls with `kind` (`policy`, `aux` or `judge`).

<a id="pt-mcpendpoint"></a>

### `pt.McpEndpoint`

```python
class McpEndpoint
```

The agent's env tools over MCP (the gateway's tool plane, streamable HTTP), filtered by its access.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `url` | `str` | required | The MCP server URL. |
| `headers` | `Mapping[str, str]` | `{}` | Headers to send with every MCP request. |

<a id="pt-callkind"></a>

### `pt.CallKind`

```python
CallKind = Literal["policy", "aux", "judge"]
```

What a model call is for: `policy` (the agent's turns: trained, and one step of its budget), `aux` (calls the harness makes for itself: trained, outside the budget) or `judge` (recorded for audit, never trained).

<a id="pt-toolaccess"></a>

### `pt.ToolAccess`

```python
ToolAccess = Literal["full", "no_terminal", "read_only"]
```

What an agent may do with the env's tools: everything, everything but the terminal (submit/finish) tool, or only tools that declare themselves read-only.

## Episode programs

An episode program decides how one task's rollout runs its agents and grades the result. The default program, `single`, runs the environment's harness on the root agent and grades the session.

<a id="pt-program"></a>

### `pt.program`

```python
def program(name: str, *, version: str = "1") -> Callable[[EpisodeProgram], EpisodeProgram]
```

Register the decorated `async def fn(ep: EpisodeContext) -> Outcome` as episode program `name@version`.

An environment config runs it with `program: name` (or `name@version` when several versions are
registered): through an installed `platoon.programs` entry point named `name`, or after the entry's
`package` imports its module.  The name follows platoon's naming rule (`<owner>-<name>`, lower case;
`platoon-*`, `single` and `gym` are core's).  Registering the same function again (a re-imported module)
is allowed; another function under a registered `name@version` is an error.

<a id="pt-episodecontext"></a>

### `pt.EpisodeContext`

```python
class EpisodeContext(Protocol)
```

One rollout of one task, as a program sees it.

`behavior_judge` (verifier grading of children) and `tool_transform` (rewrites the MCP tool listing of
every agent, `platoon.gateway.mcp.bind_agent_tools`) may be set before `run`.  `root` is the root
agent's record (`platoon.gateway.AgentSession`: its misc, result and calls), e.g. for self-graded harnesses.

| Attribute | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `task` | `Task` | The task the rollout works on. |
| `session` | `EnvSession` | The rollout's environment session. |
| `config` | `RolloutConfig` | The rollout config. |
| `route` | `EnvironmentRoute` | The environment entry the task came from: its harness, program, options and subagent settings. |
| `root` | `AgentSession` | The root agent's record: its misc, result and calls. |
| `behavior_judge` | `SubagentBehaviorJudge \| None` | Judges children for verifier grading; set it before `run`. |
| `tool_transform` | `Callable[..., Any] \| None` | Rewrites the MCP tool listing of every agent; set it before `run`. |
| `judges` | `bool` | Whether this rollout's judges run (the rollout config's `judges`, which `platoon eval` sets from `inference.judges`). While they are off, `judge_endpoint` and `judge` calls are refused (`platoon.gateway.JudgesOffError`) and verifiers do not run: a program that judges reads it and does without. |

#### `EpisodeContext.run`

```python
async def run(
    harness: str | None = None,
    *,
    goal: str | None = None,
    options: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> AgentResult
```

Run the root agent: `harness` (default: the route's) on `goal` (default: the instruction).

#### `EpisodeContext.grade`

```python
async def grade() -> Outcome
```

Grade the session, failing closed (a grader that raises is an `error` outcome).

#### `EpisodeContext.judge_endpoint`

```python
def judge_endpoint() -> ModelEndpoint
```

A model endpoint on a `judge`-role agent under the root: recorded for audit, never trained.  Refused
with `platoon.gateway.JudgesOffError` while `judges` is false.

#### `EpisodeContext.add_finalizer`

```python
def add_finalizer(fn: Finalizer) -> None
```

Run `fn` on the rollout's `TrajectoryCollection` once it is built, before it is returned.

Finalizers run in the order they were added; adding the same finalizer again does nothing.

#### `EpisodeContext.snapshot`

```python
def snapshot() -> TrajectoryCollection
```

The agent tree recorded so far, as a `TrajectoryCollection` (the root's trajectory first).

It is built by the trace that builds the rollout's result (`platoon.gateway.trace`), with a placeholder
episode outcome (`scored`, reward 0, reason `snapshot`) for the root and every agent without an outcome
of its own, e.g. for a judge that reads a child's lineage mid-episode.  Nothing is closed or changed, and
the result is unaffected; the snapshot shares annotation values with the live records, so treat it as
read-only.

<a id="pt-episodeprogram"></a>

### `pt.EpisodeProgram`

```python
EpisodeProgram = Callable[[EpisodeContext], Awaitable["Outcome"]]
```

An episode program: `async def program(ep: EpisodeContext) -> Outcome`.

## Environments

The environment-service contract: a service lists tasks and opens one session per rollout; a session offers tools, grading and forks, and grades into an `Outcome`. A named environment (`EnvironmentEntry`) says once how to run one, for configs to select with `env:`.

<a id="pt-environmentservice"></a>

### `pt.EnvironmentService`

```python
class EnvironmentService(Protocol)
```

A source of tasks that opens sessions for rollouts.

A service may also have two async methods, which are optional and so not part of the protocol's runtime
check: `list_splits()`, its split names, and `list_task_names(split)`, each task's name by task id, for a
service whose task names are not its task ids.  An environment entry's `exclude_tasks` matches task names
through `list_task_names`, and looks for a task that the listed splits do not hold in the other splits that
`list_splits` names.

It may also have `check_tasks(split, task_ids)`, async and optional too: it raises an `env_config`
`EnvSetupError` for tasks among `task_ids` that it would refuse to run, which a run calls once
`exclude_tasks` left those of `split` it keeps, so that the run stops at its start.  And two synchronous
ones for deadlines on whole rollouts: `rollout_overhead_s(task_id) -> float`, the seconds a rollout of the task
may take beyond its harness's time limit, such as starting sandboxes and running a verifier, which those
deadlines add (`platoon.train.components.rollout_overhead_s`); and
`agent_timeout_s(task_id) -> float | None`, the task's own time limit for its agent (its sessions'
`agent_timeout_s`), which they count when the rollout sets no `timeout`
(`platoon.train.components.harness_time_limit_s`), as long as the service has `rollout_overhead_s`.

| Attribute | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `str` | The service's name. |

#### `EnvironmentService.list_tasks`

```python
async def list_tasks(split: str) -> list[str]
```

The ids of the tasks in `split`.

#### `EnvironmentService.get_task`

```python
async def get_task(task_id: str) -> Task
```

Load one task by id.

#### `EnvironmentService.open`

```python
async def open(task: Task, *, rollout_id: str) -> EnvSession
```

Open a session on `task` for one rollout; a setup failure raises `EnvSetupError`.

A service whose sessions have a sandbox may also take `needs`: what the rollout's harness needs from that
sandbox (`SessionNeeds`).  `open_session` passes them to a service that takes the keyword, and
opens the sessions of one that does not, such as a service that predates `needs`, without them.

<a id="pt-envsession"></a>

### `pt.EnvSession`

```python
class EnvSession(Protocol)
```

One rollout's live view of a task.

A session may set `manages_concurrency = True` (an optional attribute, so it is not part of the protocol's
runtime check): its `call_tool` then takes calls from any number of agents at once, on the session and its
shared forks, and orders them on the live env itself.  ORS and Harbor sessions do, through their live env's
gate (`platoon.envs.gate`).  The tool plane (`platoon.gateway.mcp`) calls such a session directly,
naming the calling agent (`platoon.envs.gate.on_behalf_of`), and any other one call at a time per tool
provider.

A session with a sandbox may also set `network_isolated = True` (optional too): its sandbox has no network,
so a harness placed in it could not reach the model gateway on loopback.  The harness runner then reaches the
gateway through the sandbox's route (`session.sandbox.routes["gateway"]`, which the session's
`SessionNeeds` asked for), and refuses to start a harness there without one.  A session may likewise set
`host_loopback` (optional): whether its sandbox shares this host's network, where the gateway listens on
loopback.  The runner refuses to place a harness in a sandbox that does not (`host_loopback = False`) and has
no route; a session that does not say keeps the earlier rule, that a sandbox with a network shares the host's.
A session may also give `agent_timeout_s` (optional): the task's own time limit for its agent in seconds, or
None, which harness rollouts cap the root's harness with, as they do with the rollout's `timeout`.

| Attribute | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `task` | `Task` | The task of the session. |
| `instruction` | `str` | The instruction the root agent starts from. |
| `sandbox` | `Sandbox \| None` | A task sandbox that harnesses can run in with their own (native) tools, or None. |

#### `EnvSession.tools`

```python
async def tools() -> list[ToolSpec]
```

Env tools for harnesses that do not act natively.

#### `EnvSession.call_tool`

```python
async def call_tool(name: str, arguments: dict[str, Any]) -> ToolResult
```

Call one env tool.

#### `EnvSession.grade`

```python
async def grade() -> Outcome
```

Grade the current state; infra failures return error/invalid outcomes instead of raising.

#### `EnvSession.fork`

```python
async def fork(mode: ForkMode = "shared", *, task: Task | None = None) -> EnvSession
```

A session for a child agent: `shared` (the same live state), `copy` (a copy of it) or `fresh` (a new
session), on `task` when given.

#### `EnvSession.close`

```python
async def close() -> None
```

Release the session's resources; idempotent.

<a id="pt-sessionneeds"></a>

### `pt.SessionNeeds`

```python
class SessionNeeds
```

What the harness drawn for a rollout needs from the session's sandbox; the rollout computes it before the
sandbox starts, and `EnvironmentService.open` applies it to the sandbox it opens (`apply`).

`upstreams` are the host services the harness's processes must reach (`{"gateway": "unix:///…/gw.sock"}`:
`SandboxSpec.upstreams`, answered by `Sandbox.routes`); `mounts` are binds such as the harness's toolchain,
read-only at its build path; `extra_memory_mb` is the memory of the harness's own processes (its spec's
`[resources] memory_mb`), added to the sandbox's memory limit when it has one.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `upstreams` | `Mapping[str, str]` | `{}` | Upstream name -> a host endpoint the harness's processes must reach (SandboxSpec.upstreams). |
| `mounts` | `tuple[Mount, ...]` | `()` | Binds the harness needs, such as its toolchain, read-only at its build path. |
| `extra_memory_mb` | `int` | `0` | The memory of the harness's own processes, added to the sandbox's memory limit when it has one. |

#### `SessionNeeds.apply`

```python
def apply(spec: SandboxSpec) -> SandboxSpec
```

`spec` with these needs: their upstreams and mounts added (a mount whose target the spec already binds
keeps the spec's), and the memory limit grown.

<a id="pt-outcome"></a>

### `pt.Outcome`

```python
class Outcome
```

The graded result of a session; only `scored` outcomes train.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `status` | `OutcomeStatus` | required | `scored` (a valid measurement), `invalid`, `error`, `timeout` or `cancelled`. |
| `rewards` | `dict[str, float]` | `{}` | Named reward components. |
| `primary` | `str` | `"reward"` | The component that is the reward; a scored outcome must have it. |
| `reason` | `str \| None` | `None` | Why the outcome is what it is, e.g. "no_submit", "judge_unavailable". |
| `failure_kind` | `str \| None` | `None` | The infrastructure failure class of an `error` or `invalid` outcome. |
| `metadata` | `dict[str, Any]` | `{}` | The grader's structured detail. |
| `reward` | `float \| None` | | The primary reward of a scored outcome; None otherwise. Read-only. |
| `trainable` | `bool` | | Whether the outcome is `scored`, the only status that trains. Read-only. |

#### `Outcome.infra`

```python
@classmethod
def infra(
    failure_kind: str,

```

An untrainable outcome for a failure that says nothing about the policy.

<a id="pt-toolspec"></a>

### `pt.ToolSpec`

```python
class ToolSpec
```

An env tool for harnesses that do not act natively; `input_schema` is a JSON schema.

The hints drive tool access (filtering happens in the harness layer and the
MCP plane): a `terminal` tool ends the episode (submit, claim_done), so
agents with `no_terminal` access do not see it; a `read_only` tool never
changes env state, and only such tools reach `read_only` agents. `meta`
passes provider metadata through as MCP `_meta` (for example
`openhands.dev/tool-routing`).

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `str` | required |  |
| `description` | `str` | required |  |
| `input_schema` | `dict[str, Any]` | required |  |
| `terminal` | `bool` | `False` | The tool ends the episode (submit, finish). |
| `read_only` | `bool` | `False` | The tool never changes env state. |
| `meta` | `Mapping[str, Any] \| None` | `None` | Provider metadata, passed through as MCP `_meta`. |

<a id="pt-toolresult"></a>

### `pt.ToolResult`

```python
class ToolResult
```

An env tool's reply as MCP-style content blocks, plus the episode signals some envs send.

`finished` says the env ended the episode, `reward` is the reward the
env attached to this call, and `metadata` is the env's structured detail
(`{"invalid": true}` marks a grade the env declares invalid).

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `content` | `list[dict[str, Any]]` | required | MCP content blocks, such as `{"type": "text", "text": ...}`. |
| `is_error` | `bool` | `False` | The call failed; the content says why. |
| `finished` | `bool` | `False` |  |
| `reward` | `float \| None` | `None` |  |
| `metadata` | `dict[str, Any]` | `{}` |  |

#### `ToolResult.text`

```python
@classmethod

```

A result with one text block.

#### `ToolResult.as_text`


The content as one string: text blocks joined by newlines, other blocks as placeholders.

<a id="pt-environmententry"></a>

### `pt.EnvironmentEntry`

```python
class EnvironmentEntry
```

A named environment: `name@version` and the partial `environments` entry it stands for.

`EnvironmentEntry(name, version="1", *, description="", harness_defaults=None, **keys)`, where `keys` are
keys of an `environments` entry (`service`, `service_kwargs`, `harness`, `program`,
`reward_processor`, `agents`, `dataset_kwargs`, ...), checked against the config schema when the entry
is built.  A run chooses the rest (`FORBIDDEN_KEYS`): `env`, `name`, `weight`, `task_sampler` and
`task_sampler_options`, `group_admission` and `group_admission_options`, `max_staleness`, the run-level
settings, the tasks it leaves out (`exclude_tasks`; an environment that should not offer a task leaves it out of
its own task lists, in a new version), `harness_options`, for which `harness_defaults` maps a harness name to
the options the environment needs from that harness, of `workflow_config` all but the rollout settings
(`rollout_config`) its tasks were measured with, and `eval_overrides.workflow_config`.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `str` | required | The environment's name, `<owner>-<name>`. |
| `version` | `str` | `"1"` | Bumped when the tasks, the grading or the defaults change. |
| `description` | `str` | `""` | One line saying what the environment is, for listings. |
| `harness_defaults` | `Mapping[str, Mapping[str, Any]]` | `{}` | Harness name -> the lowest layer of that harness's `harness_options` on this environment. |
| `keys` | `Mapping[str, Any]` | `{}` | The partial environments entry: the keyword arguments other than the fields above. |
| `ref` | `str` | | `name@version`, what a config pins with `env:`. Read-only. |

#### `EnvironmentEntry.entry`

```python
def entry() -> dict[str, Any]
```

The partial environments entry, as a fresh copy.

#### `EnvironmentEntry.defaults_for`

```python
def defaults_for(harness: Any) -> dict[str, Any]
```

The `harness_defaults` of the entry's `harness` (a reference, or a `{harness: weight}` mixture), as a
fresh copy; empty when it has none.  A `.toml` path or `module:function` reference matches no name.

A mixture of several harnesses shares one `harness_options` mapping, so a mixture that includes a harness
with defaults raises `ValueError`.

## Gym adapters

Adapters from reset/step environments to harnesses and ORS environments.

<a id="pt-gym"></a>

### `pt.gym`

Gym adapters: step environments as a function harness, or as an ORS environment with one `act` tool.

A *step env* is the classic reset/step loop over text:

    class StepEnv(Protocol):
        async def reset(self, task: Task) -> str: ...                        # the first observation
        async def step(self, action: str) -> tuple[str, float, bool]: ...    # observation, reward, done

* `loop` turns one into a function harness that alternates model calls and `env.step`: the model's
  reply text is the action, the observation is the next user message.  The step env lives inside the harness,
  so it grades itself: the return (the sum of the step rewards, the gym convention) is recorded in the agent's
  misc under `gym_return`, and the `gym` program scores the episode with it.
* `as_environment` wraps one as an openreward `Environment` subclass whose single `act` tool steps
  it, so any harness plays it through a tool and the ORS grading path scores it: every result carries the return
  so far as its reward, so the call that ends the episode grades it with the return, and so does the
  `max_tool_calls` cap.  It works with openreward 0.1.125 (`tool(fn=None, *, shared=True)`) and later.

When the agent's budget runs out before the episode ends, `loop` is scored with the return so far, and so
is `as_environment` at its session's `max_tool_calls`; an `act` episode that the agent leaves unfinished
otherwise (its own step budget ran out first) is graded as any ORS episode without a finished result: 0,
`no_submit`.

<a id="pt-gym-gym-return-misc-key"></a>

#### `pt.gym.GYM_RETURN_MISC_KEY`

```python
GYM_RETURN_MISC_KEY = "gym_return"
```

The agent misc key under which `loop` records the episode's return.

<a id="pt-gym-stepenv"></a>

#### `pt.gym.StepEnv`

```python
class StepEnv(Protocol)
```

A reset/step environment over text.  An optional `close` (sync or async) is called when it is done.

##### `StepEnv.reset`

```python
async def reset(task: Task) -> str
```

Start an episode of `task`; return the first observation.

##### `StepEnv.step`

```python
async def step(action: str) -> tuple[str, float, bool]
```

Apply `action`; return the observation, the step reward and whether the episode is done.

<a id="pt-gym-as-environment"></a>

#### `pt.gym.as_environment`

```python
def as_environment(
    env_factory: Callable[[], StepEnv],
    *,
    name: str,
    tasks: Mapping[str, Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]]] | None = None,
) -> type
```

An openreward `Environment` subclass named `name` that serves `env_factory()` through `act`.

`tasks` maps each split to its task specs (default: one `train` task `{"id": "0"}`); a task spec's
`goal` and `id` become the `Task` the step env is reset with, and the whole spec its `misc`.  Each
`act` result carries the return so far as its reward, and the step's own reward and the return in its
metadata (`step_reward`, `return`).

<a id="pt-gym-gym-program"></a>

#### `pt.gym.gym_program`

```python
async def gym_program(ep: EpisodeContext) -> Outcome
```

Run the root agent and score it with the return its `gym.loop` harness recorded.

A root that failed (error, timeout, cancellation) keeps the usual untrainable outcome; a harness that
recorded no return is graded by the env session.

<a id="pt-gym-loop"></a>

#### `pt.gym.loop`

```python
def loop(
    env_factory: Callable[[], StepEnv],
    *,
    max_turns: int | None = None,
    system: str | None = None,
) -> AgentFn
```

A function harness that plays `env_factory()` turn by turn (register it with `@pt.harness`).

The loop ends when the env says `done` (`completed`), or with `limit` and the out-of-budget warning
(`LIMIT_MESSAGE`) after `max_turns` turns or when the agent's step budget or `ctx.max_steps` runs out.
`system` is an optional system message.  Each step is annotated with its action, observation and reward.

## Deprecations

A form that a later release removes, such as a config key, keeps working for one minor release with a warning that names what replaces it and the release that removes it.

<a id="pt-platoondeprecationwarning"></a>

### `pt.PlatoonDeprecationWarning`

```python
class PlatoonDeprecationWarning(FutureWarning)
```

A form platoon still accepts, such as a config key, that a later release removes.

Each warning names what replaces the form and the release that removes it. It is a `FutureWarning`, which
Python shows by default, unlike a `DeprecationWarning` outside `__main__`. `platoon config validate --strict` fails on a config that uses a deprecated key, and in Python
`warnings.simplefilter("error", pt.PlatoonDeprecationWarning)` (or pytest's
`-W error::platoon.PlatoonDeprecationWarning`) turns the warnings into errors.
